title: The Last Homecoming
premise: Rosalind Underhill has spent senior year keeping her head down, raising her younger siblings while her mother works nights, counting the days until graduation frees her. When her best friend Priya vanishes, leaving only a carabiner of keys on the school bleachers, Rosalind's careful invisibility shatters: the keys belong to a storage unit holding evidence that Coach Danvers, the town's beloved football hero, has been exploiting and blackmailing students for years. As Rosalind investigates, she learns Priya stayed silent to protect a scholarship—and that Rosalind's own silence made her complicit. In the end, Rosalind chooses justice over safety, exposing Danvers at the championship game even though it costs her the friendship she was trying to save, because Priya, found alive but broken, can no longer trust the friend who looked away.
about_author: Odile Thackeray is a former high school counselor who spent a decade listening to students describe the things adults refused to hear. She writes from a converted garage in upstate New York, where she lives with two rescue dogs and an unreasonable number of houseplants.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Days
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A morning in the Underhill household: packing lunches, waking siblings, covering for Mom's night shift. At school, Rosalind counts down to graduation while Priya teases her for being invisible on purpose. Emotional beat: weary competence masking a hunger to be seen.

chapters.title: Keys on the Bleachers
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Priya misses their Friday ritual; her texts stop mid-sentence. Rosalind finds a carabiner of unfamiliar keys taped under the bleachers with a note bearing only her name. The police shrug—runaway, probably. Emotional beat: dread arriving quietly, like weather.

chapters.title: What Runaways Leave Behind
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind searches Priya's locker and bedroom, finding no packed bag, no note home. Priya's mother is too grief-fogged to help. Rosalind notices the keys are stamped with a storage facility logo across town. Emotional beat: the first crack in official stories.

chapters.title: Unit 114
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Using the keys, Rosalind opens Unit 114: boxes of letters, cash ledgers, and photos of students—including Priya—dated over years. She recognizes Coach Danvers' handwriting. She takes one photo and flees. Emotional beat: terror fused with purpose.

chapters.title: The Golden Boy of Halloway
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Flashback chapter: how Danvers built his empire of favors, scholarships, and silence, and how the whole town worships him before Friday games. Rosalind realizes Priya's athletic scholarship hung on his word. Emotional beat: admiration curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Little Adults
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Home life frays as Rosalind's investigation eats her attention; her brother Marcus covers for her once too often and they fight. Mom picks up another shift. Emotional beat: guilt—the cost of caring about something beyond survival.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Knew
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind confronts teammate Jess, who goes pale at Danvers' name and denies everything too fast. Later, an anonymous text warns Rosalind to return what she took. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root; allies may be informants.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind deciphers the ledgers with Marcus's math-nerd help: payments routed through a booster club shell. The pattern implicates a vice principal too. Emotional beat: the corruption is bigger than one man—a system, not a villain.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Homecoming week; the town celebrates Danvers' twenty years. Rosalind attends, watching everyone cheer the man she suspects, and nearly breaks when Danvers greets her warmly by name. Emotional beat: isolation inside a crowd.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind tracks down a graduated victim, Dana, now working double shifts at a diner. Dana confirms everything but refuses to go public: 'I paid my price. You pay yours.' Emotional beat: understanding why victims stay quiet—and refusing to accept it.

chapters.title: Caught Looking
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Danvers corners Rosalind after practice, offering a college recommendation in exchange for the photo. He mentions her siblings' school by name. Threat wrapped in kindness. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: What Marcus Found
chapters.summary: POV Marcus (first shift). Marcus, digging deeper online, discovers the storage unit is rented under Priya's name—she was building her own case before she vanished. Emotional beat: sibling partnership forged; Priya wasn't just a victim but a fighter.

chapters.title: The Missing Week
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Reconstructing Priya's last week through bus cameras and a diner receipt, Rosalind learns Priya met someone at the unit the night she disappeared—and it wasn't Danvers. Emotional beat: the mystery pivots; not everything is what the evidence suggested.

chapters.title: Jess Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Jess confesses: Danvers pressured her last year, and Priya knew and confronted him. Jess stayed silent to keep her roster spot. Rosalind's fury at her own past silence meets Jess's shame. Emotional beat: complicity acknowledged, forgiveness withheld—for now.

chapters.title: A Deal with the Devil's Assistant
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The vice principal offers Rosalind a quiet trade: the photo for a full-ride scholarship and Priya's safe return 'arranged.' Rosalind realizes they know where Priya is. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive—everything she wants, bought with silence.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind tails the vice principal to a motel outside town and finds Priya, hiding voluntarily—scared, ashamed, gathering courage to testify. They reconcile bitterly: Priya's anger at Rosalind's years of looking away is the chapter's wound. Emotional beat: reunion without absolution.

chapters.title: Truth Has a Tuition
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Priya agrees to come forward only if Rosalind testifies too—admitting she saw warning signs and said nothing. Rosalind weighs her siblings' safety against the debt she owes. Emotional beat: accepting that justice requires self-indictment.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Championship night. During halftime, with the town assembled, Rosalind takes the microphone and tells everything—naming Danvers, the vice principal, and her own silence. The gym goes silent, then erupts. Emotional beat: climax; terror transfigured into voice.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Fallout: Danvers arrested, the school board scrambling, half the town blaming Rosalind, Marcus and the little ones proud. Mom comes home early from a shift for the first time in years. Emotional beat: the cost made visible, and worth it.

chapters.title: What Friendship Costs
chapters.summary: POV Priya (shift). Priya, recovering at home, reads Rosalind's letter admitting every failure. She doesn't forgive yet—but she sends back the carabiner of keys, a message that the door isn't locked forever. Emotional beat: grief and hope sharing a room.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Graduation arrives; Rosalind walks the stage having lost the easy future but gained a real one. Dana from the diner appears in the crowd, nodding. Jess stands beside her. Emotional beat: earned peace, imperfect but true.

chapters.title: The Next Homecoming
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, epilogue. One year later: Rosalind, working part-time and pre-law bound, visits Unit 114, now empty, and leaves flowers. Priya texts: coffee? Rosalind says yes. Emotional beat: resolution—survival redefined as living, not just enduring.
